chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: His songs and the singers who never recorded them
summary: He has written many tunes, handed copies to people who never performed them, and would like Johnny Hodges to play some.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You've written a lot of tunes.
But none of them have had no success with (?).
Well, I always thought maybe some of them would be very fine if they were done by a singer.
Yeah, well, they should have been done by a singer.
Did you ever take any of them to some people who might use them?
Well, I don't know. I have asked some people about them; you know, putting them like to sing(?) and stuff. They say, 'Yeah,' you know. But never did it.
I've handed out several copies of my songs to people, but I've never heard them done. So that shows you that my songs are pretty bad!
Like 'I'll Try'? That's a beautiful song!
It's the way you do it.
Well, a couple of songs, I would like to have had Johnny Hodges play them. Because I could hear him playing the song when I wrote it, you know.
